high_critical.task: Place a shaded water bowl for strays in your area
high_critical.why: With today's heat conditions, animals outdoors can dehydrate quickly. A shaded bowl stays cooler and more accessible.

high_critical.task: Refill an existing outdoor water source for street animals
high_critical.why: Water evaporates and heats up faster on high-heat days. Refilling ensures cool hydration is available.

high_critical.task: Move any visible animal water bowl out of direct sunlight
high_critical.why: Direct sun heats water significantly. Cool water encourages drinking and prevents further overheating.

high_critical.task: Keep a shallow tray of water for birds near shade
high_critical.why: Birds also suffer from heat stress and dehydration. Shallow water allows safe drinking and cooling.

high_critical.task: Report any collapsed or heavily panting stray animal you observe
high_critical.why: In critical heat, animals can deteriorate within minutes. Early reporting allows faster response.

high_critical.task: Do not disturb resting strays in shaded areas â€” let them rest
high_critical.why: Resting in shade is a survival behaviour in heat. Disturbing them forces re-exertion in dangerous conditions.

moderate.task: Refill your neighbourhood's animal water bowl if you pass one
moderate.why: Moderate heat still requires consistent hydration access for outdoor animals.

moderate.task: Add a bird water tray to your balcony, garden, or terrace
moderate.why: Bird populations benefit significantly from accessible water during warm months.

moderate.task: Ensure any water bowl you have is in the shade, not sun
moderate.why: Sun-exposed water heats quickly and becomes less beneficial or even discouraging to drink.

low.task: Maintain and clean an existing outdoor water source
low.why: Clean water prevents bacterial growth and keeps animals healthy even in lower risk conditions.

low.task: Check if any outdoor water containers are empty and refill them
low.why: Even on cooler days, outdoor animals need consistent hydration.
